mechanics.name: Buckle Up
mechanics.currentEffect: While healing a Survivor in the Dying State, you both see the Killer's Aura. When you finish healing them into the Injured State, the healed Survivor leaves no Scratch Marks and gains 50% Haste for 3/4/5 seconds.
activation: Heal another Survivor from the Dying State to Injured.
Ends/deactivates when: Killer Aura reading applies while the healing interaction is in progress.
Ends/deactivates when: Haste and Scratch Mark suppression end after 3/4/5 seconds.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.0.0): Reworked the perk to its current Dying-State healing and post-heal Haste effect.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Healing a downed teammate reveals the Killer, then gives the rescued teammate a brief Haste burst and hides their Scratch Marks.
duration: Post-heal Haste and no Scratch Marks: 3/4/5 seconds.
specialInteractions: Both you and the healed Survivor see the Killer's Aura while healing a Survivor in the Dying State.

editorial.summary: While healing a downed teammate, both of you can see the Killer; completing the pickup gives the rescued Survivor a strong Haste burst and hides their Scratch Marks.
useCases: Read whether the Killer is returning while you attempt a ground pickup.
Give the recovered teammate enough Haste to escape the immediate area.
Use Scratch-Mark suppression to make the revived Survivor's exit route harder to follow.
counters: The speed and stealth benefits go to the recovered Survivor, not the healer.
If the Killer hooks promptly, the perk never matters.
pros: Built-in Killer information during the risky heal.
Strong escape burst for the recovered teammate.
cons: Less powerful than older versions players may remember.
analysis: Buckle Up takes this position because the current version still has useful anti-slug value even though it no longer carries the infamous protection package of older metas. The Killer Aura during the heal tells both players whether finishing the pickup is safe.
Once the teammate reaches Injured, their Haste burst can create substantial immediate distance, while hidden Scratch Marks make the path harder to track after line of sight breaks.
The perk's weakness is opportunity. A Killer who hooks downed Survivors normally gives Buckle Up almost nothing to do. Even during slugging, the healer remains vulnerable to interruption.
That makes it a competent recovery-support perk rather than a meta staple. It works well in anti-slug builds, but does not deserve a slot in every match.
editorial.verdict: A useful modern anti-slug support perk. Buckle Up helps the recovered Survivor escape, but its old reputation should not inflate the strength of the current version.
